Independent enumeration via permutation determinants for F_2,F_3,F_5; general proof uses complete rank strata rather than finite extrapolation.
correctness.rationale: Bordering the 3×3 Hankel B gives det H=(det B)a6−vᵀadj(B)v. Invertible B contributes q^6−q^5 to every t. For det B=0 and top-left δ=a0a2−a1²≠0, adj(B)=δnnᵀ yields a squared linear form; direct summation of ρ2(−t/δ) using m_q(δ)=q²+q(ρ2(−δ)−1) gives q^4(q−1)+q³(q−1)(ρ2(t)−1). In the remaining rank-2 δ=0 cases, A=a0≠0 gives det H=−Ah³ and q³(q−1) solutions for t≠0, whereas a0=0,a3≠0 gives det H=a3^4 and q³ρ4(t). Rank≤1 gives the zero-fiber remainder q⁴. All terms sum to stated formula including t=0, no forbidden division at zero. Independent direct permutation-determinant enumeration over q=2,3,5 agrees with every fiber (q=2:64,64; q=3:729,810,648; q=5:15625,16500,15000,15000,16000); finite counts corroborate but do not prove all prime powers.

evidence: García-Armas–Ghorpade–Ram arXiv:1011.1760 Thm.5.1 counts nonsingularity by rank; Dwivedi–Grinberg arXiv:2109.05415 Thm.1.5 and Cor.1.7 refine rank with prescribed initial coefficients, not the distribution of det=t≠0. A general theorem determining the full value distribution was not identified in the full primary materials inspected.

originality.rationale: Classical Daykin and García-Armas–Ghorpade–Ram work enumerates Hankel ranks/zero determinant; Dwivedi–Grinberg prescribes initial coefficients and Hankel rank. The result refines these by nonzero determinant values and quadratic/fourth-power residue types, which cannot be reconstructed from rank counts.

The count is for unrestricted ordered coefficient septuples over fields, not symmetry classes.
